DOCUMENT S04 — Little Barford power station shift account, 9 August 2019
Owner/originator: RWE Generation, Little Barford station operating staff (roles only; no individuals)
Record type: reconstructed shift narrative, known/unknown summary and investigation status addendum
STATUS: SYNTHESISED FOR EVALUATION — NOT REAL EVIDENCE. Reconstructed from published investigation
material for this exercise; wording, layout and record structure are reconstructions.
Clock reference: BST (UTC+01:00). This account adds no clock readings; it gives only the approximate
intervals stated in the published sources, and each interval names the event it is measured from.
Value-status legend: [reported] value as stated in published material; [illustrative] texture only,
never a time, MW value or cause (not used in this account); [measured] and [estimated] not used.
Roles: "plant operators" and "operating staff" refer to the station's operational staff on shift.

PART 1 — SHIFT NARRATIVE (reconstructed from published accounts)
Plant state before the disturbance
N1  The station (740 MW [reported] CCGT, connected at Eaton Socon 400 kV [reported] substation) had
    all three units operating: gas turbines GT1A and GT1B and steam turbine ST1C.
Steam turbine trip
N2  Within 1 second [reported] of the lightning strike and the resulting transmission system disturbance,
    steam turbine ST1C tripped while generating 244 MW [reported].
N3  At the start of the station's event sequence the 110 V AC UPS -B- and then UPS -A- raised general
    fault alarms (station sequence-of-events record).
Steam bypass operation
N4  With the steam turbine lost, the plant went into steam bypass mode: steam generated from the gas
    turbines is fed directly into the condenser. This is the normal operation following loss of the
    steam turbine, intended to allow sustained operation of the gas turbines.
N5  Following the steam turbine trip, the pressure in the steam system rose.
First gas turbine trip
N6  Around a minute [reported] after the transmission system fault, gas turbine GT1A (generating
    210 MW [reported]) tripped automatically due to a high-pressure excursion in the steam bypass system.
Second gas turbine trip
N7  The steam system pressure continued to rise after the GT1A trip, and the plant operators made the
    decision to manually trip the other operational gas turbine due to safety risks.
N8  Around 30 seconds [reported] after the GT1A trip, GT1B (187 MW [reported]) was manually tripped by
    the operating staff in response to high steam pressures. Total station loss: 641 MW [reported].

PART 2 — KNOWN AND NOT KNOWN (operator's preliminary findings of 30 August 2019, as also summarised in
the ESO technical report of 6 September 2019)
Known (trip mechanisms)
K1  ST1C: the trip was initiated by a discrepancy between the measurements from three [reported] speed
    signals, after the point of the transmission system fault clearance.
K2  GT1A: automated trip following a high-pressure excursion in the steam bypass system.
K3  GT1B: manual trip by operating staff in response to excessive steam pressure.
K4  UPS: all UPS units functioned correctly; the operator does not now believe the UPS were related to the
    subsequent trip.
Not known (underlying causes)
U1  Why the speed signals disagreed: not established. A review of hardware, software, fault handling
    and diagnostic coverage for the conditions the steam turbine was subjected to is ongoing.
U2  Why the high-pressure excursion occurred: "for reasons presently unknown" (operator).
U3  UPS: the operator's hypothesis (not an established finding) is that the UPS units changed over to
    battery back-up supplies as a consequence of the system disturbance; what characteristic of the UPS
    power supply caused the switch to battery operation is still to be determined.
Planned follow-up
F1  Physical inspection of the bypass system during the forthcoming outage in September 2019 to help
    determine the root cause of the pressure excursions.
F2  OEM resilience testing of the UPS during the outage commencing 6 September 2019 [reported].

PART 3 — INVESTIGATION STATUS ADDENDUM (compiled from later published findings; not part of the shift
record). Source: Ofgem report dated 3 January 2020.
X1  Established (Ofgem): the steam turbine tripped initially because of a discrepancy in the three [reported]
    independent speed sensors on the turbine; the discrepancy exceeded the tolerance of the control
    system, causing the generator to shut down automatically.
X2  Not established: "The root cause of the discrepancy in the speed sensors has not been established."
X3  Finding (Ofgem): after the steam turbine trip the steam system pressure rose and safety systems
    automatically shut down one gas turbine due to excessive pressure in the steam bypass; pressure
    continued to rise and the plant operators manually tripped the other gas turbine due to safety risks.
X4  Not established: "The root cause of these high pressure conditions has not been established."
X5  Regulator's preliminary view (explicitly a view, not an established cause): given the sequence of
    events and in the absence of an established root cause, the steam turbine's anomalous speed readings
    and the resulting trip were due to the transmission network fault following the lightning strike.
X6  Still a hypothesis: the operator's explanation (30 August 2019) that the UPS changed over to battery
    back-up as a consequence of the system disturbance; no later finding on it is included here.
